identity.title: Syncope while supine or seated without warning

technique.how: Ask exactly what the patient was doing and their body position when consciousness was lost: lying flat, sitting, standing, or during exertion. Ask specifically whether there was any warning (nausea, warmth, sweating, tunnel vision) or whether it was sudden with no prodrome.
technique.prerequisites: Patient or witness recall of the circumstances of the event.

interpretation.positive_finding: Syncope occurring while supine is uncommon (about 10% of cardiac syncope) but has a pooled LR of about 4 for a cardiac (arrhythmic) cause because reflex syncope needs an upright position.
interpretation.negative_finding: Most cardiac syncope occurs upright, so absence of supine syncope (LR- ~0.9) does not lower the probability of a cardiac cause.
interpretation.pitfalls: Seated syncope is less specific than truly supine syncope and was not separately quantified; supine events with a typical vasovagal prodrome (e.g., during venepuncture) can still be reflex. Confirm the patient was not simply found lying down after falling.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: treat as high-risk syncope - ECG, telemetry/monitoring, echo and cardiology review; negative: no change.

estimates.target_condition: Cardiac (arrhythmic or structural) syncope vs non-cardiac syncope (finding: syncope in the supine position)
estimates.population: Pooled derivation sample from published syncope cohorts reporting supine syncope (3 studies; 170 cardiac and 507 non-cardiac syncope patients)
estimates.reference_standard: Final cause of syncope by each study's standardized diagnostic criteria (ESC-based work-up, EP study/tilt where used)
estimates.computed_from: Table 2 counts: supine syncope in 17/170 (10%) cardiac vs 12/507 (2%) non-cardiac. Sens=17/170=0.10; spec=495/507=0.976; LR+ 4.23 as printed in Table 2 LR column (=0.10/0.0237); LR-=0.90/0.976=0.92 (computed). Chi-square 18.1, p<0.0001.
estimates.location: Table 2 (Supine syncope row), PMC3815402 open-access full text

sources.citation: Berecki-Gisolf J, Sheldon A, Wieling W, et al. Identifying cardiac syncope based on clinical history: a literature-based model tested in four independent datasets. PLoS One. 2013;8(11):e75255.
Albassam OT, Redelmeier RJ, Shadowitz S, Husain AM, Simel D, Etchells EE. Did This Patient Have Cardiac Syncope? The Rational Clinical Examination Systematic Review. JAMA. 2019;321(24):2448-2457.
Alboni P, Brignole M, Menozzi C, et al. Diagnostic value of history in patients with syncope with or without heart disease. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2001;37(7):1921-1928.
Del Rosso A, Ungar A, Maggi R, et al. Clinical predictors of cardiac syncope at initial evaluation in patients referred urgently to a general hospital: the EGSYS score. Heart. 2008;94(12):1620-1626.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use the absence of supine syncope to classify an event as benign; upright syncope is the norm for both reflex and cardiac causes.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Supine or exertional syncope without prodrome, particularly with heart disease, abnormal ECG or family history of sudden death, warrants monitored observation and urgent cardiology assessment.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Body position at onset is usually reported consistently, but 'no warning' is subjective and depends on recall (retrograde amnesia is common after syncope).

extraction_notes: Anchor RCE (Albassam 2019) is not open access and its abstract does not report a supine-syncope estimate; the number here comes from the open-access Berecki-Gisolf 2013 literature-based model (Table 2), which pooled counts from the 3 derivation studies that reported supine syncope (Table 2 shows non-blank columns for 3 studies). Quote is the verbatim Table 2 row (per-study columns, totals, chi-square, df, p, LR). Sens/spec and LR- are computed from the printed counts; LR+ 4.23 is as printed. Alboni 2001 (abstract) names supine syncope among the most specific predictors of cardiac cause in patients with heart disease and EGSYS (Del Rosso 2008) includes 'syncope in supine position' as a score item, but neither abstract gives item-level numbers and full texts are not accessible. 'Seated' syncope and 'without warning' (absent prodrome) were not separately quantified here; brief/absent prodrome is a distinct Berecki-Gisolf variable (long prodrome LR for absence 1.66) not entered because it is a different discriminator.
